newsitem.title: SPAIN: ETA frees kidnapped Basque businessman.
newsitem.headline: ETA frees kidnapped Basque businessman.

text.p: The Basque guerrilla group ETA freed kidnapped Basque businessman Cosme Delclaux early on Tuesday, police said.
Delclaux, 34, had been held captive for 232 days and Spanish media reported last month that his family had paid a ransom for his release.

Delclaux was found tied to a tree in the Basque province of Vizcaya in the early hours of Tuesday after the newspaper EGIN, which is closely tied to ETA, received an anonymous phone call informing it of his release, Spanish news agencies reported.
He was taken to a Vizcaya police station. Spanish media reports said Delclaux was healthy but disoriented and sleepy.

Spain's centre-right government has insisted that no peace talks with ETA were possible as long as the group holds hostages. ETA is also believed to be holding a former prison worker Jose Antonio Ortega Lara, missing for nearly two years.

Delclaux was kidnapped on his way home from work in a technological park on November 11, 1996 in the Basque country where businessmen have long complained that ETA runs a campaign of extortion aimed at them.
Delclaux is a lawyer and the son of a wealthy and well-known Basque industrialist.
ETA, which stands for Basque Homeland and Freedom, has waged a 29-year struggle for independence from Spain in which 800 people have been killed.
